steps: Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan about 1 minute until fragrant, then grind. Set aside.
Pan-fry the tofu cubes in a little oil until lightly golden on two sides; set aside. (Skip this and use silken tofu for a softer, more mapo-like texture.)
Soffritto: olive oil, onion, carrot and celery, about 8 minutes until soft. Add garlic and ginger, 1 minute more.
Add the ground beef and brown well, breaking it up.
Stir in the tomato paste, 1 minute. Deglaze with the red wine and let it reduce.
Add the tomatoes, stock, soy sauce, half the ground Sichuan pepper and the chilli flakes. Simmer 25-30 minutes until thick.
Fold in the tofu and simmer gently 5-8 minutes so it soaks up the sauce -- stir softly so the cubes stay whole.
Boil the pasta al dente, then toss with the sauce and a splash of pasta water.
Finish with the remaining Sichuan pepper, spring onion and parmesan.
notes: Italian-Chinese fusion, family experiment: a proper bolognese base (soffritto, browned beef, long tomato simmer) with tofu folded in and a kick of toasted Sichuan pepper and soy sauce, served over pasta.
